extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — grant applicants, investigators, institutional research administrators, and other stakeholders in NIH funding
extracted.subtask_description: A landing/news page summarizing recent NIH announcements, resources, and reminders relevant to preparing, submitting, and understanding NIH grant applications and policies. Items include guidance on model selection, data management plan formats, reproducibility expectations, review outcomes, and program updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select models appropriate to research questions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches, including New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), and encourages approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, but investigators must justify that the chosen models best address their research question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow PF5 application format and understand linked-award splitting
rubrics_metrics.description: "Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants for PF5 should learn the specific application format and be aware that NIH may split applications into linked awards following review and prior to Just-in-Time requests; familiarity with these features is a preparatory expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans, investigators should use the 2026 pilot format and include the simplified set of required elements specified by NIH; this is a required format for applicable submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize replication and reproducibility in applications and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Embedding replication and reproducibility throughout NIH research is a key reminder for applications and awards, supported by NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan and a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to consider and, where appropriate, incorporate plans or approaches that support replication and reproducibility. NIH is incentivizing and institutionalizing replication/reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise; proposals aligning with these priorities may be viewed favorably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand 'Competitive But Not Discussed' review outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: "Last November, NIH implemented emergency modifications to review processes... the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants receiving this designation should understand it can reflect a cut (e.g., below a 33% discussion cutoff) despite being considered competitive; NIH emergency modifications affected how some applications were triaged and labeled during peer review.
